title: How Windsurf writes 90% of your code with an Agentic IDE - Kevin Hou, Windsurf
talk_summary: Kevin Hou presents Windsurf's agentic editor principles: a shared human-agent action timeline, inferred memory, and model-driven retrieval/tool use instead of explicit context. He also describes running terminal commands in the same environment with LLM safety checks and letting the model read web/docs dynamically.

takeaways.what_they_do: Windsurf records file views, edits, terminal commands, and agent actions into one shared timeline so the agent has current state and does not undo recent human work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this all kind of goes into a shared timeline of actions

takeaways.what_they_do: Windsurf infers project facts and user preferences from tool use and stores them as memories, rather than relying only on a rules file.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've implemented a concept called autogenerated Memories so over time we build up a memory bank

takeaways.what_they_do: Windsurf lets the agent plan and retrieve code/docs automatically, using explicit mentions only at the margin instead of requiring users to specify all context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 90% of the time you do not need to at mention something

takeaways.what_they_do: Windsurf lets the LLM classify terminal commands as safe or unsafe, auto-running routine commands and prompting for dangerous ones like rm -rf; users can also allow/blacklist commands.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can automatically use the llm to decide what is safe and not safe

takeaways.technique: Run commands in the same sandbox environment
takeaways.what_they_do: Windsurf executes agent commands inside the same terminal/sandbox the human would use, so installs and commands share the real environment instead of a separate background shell.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we put this right inside of the place that you would actually write terminal commands
